Agent: That's good to hear. Now, just to confirm — you do have the intention and the ability to pay once the funds arrive, correct? This is not a hardship situation where you cannot pay at all?

Customer: Haan, full amount. No problem. I will even pay extra if there is any late fee or penalty added. Just clear this off.

Agent: Hello, is this Vikram Sharma speaking? This is Rajesh calling from Credix Finance.

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Vikram. What is the matter, sir? Why are you calling?

Agent: Sir, I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4782. Our records show you're currently overdue on your EMI. Your last payment was received on the 15th of last month. Can we discuss your payment situation today?

Customer: Haan, I know, I know about this loan. Look, the thing is, sir, I'm managing so many things right now, na. Tell me, what is the outstanding amount exactly?

Agent: Of course, sir. Your current outstanding balance is Rs. 2,87,450. You have missed two EMI installments of Rs. 18,500 each. That makes it Rs. 37,000 in arrears. Are you in a position to clear this or at least make a payment today?

Customer: Two installments? I thought... <interruption> ...anyway, sir, that's not the main issue. The real problem is I'm not just managing this one loan. I have a home loan with ICICI Bank — Rs. 28,000 per month, and then Axis Bank business loan, another Rs. 5,500 per month. So my total EMI every month is coming to almost Rs. 52,000. My salary is Rs. 55,000 per month, sir. After tax deductions, I'm getting maybe Rs. 48,000 in hand. How am I supposed to manage all three at the same time, na?

Agent: I see, sir. So your EMIs are actually exceeding your take-home income. That's a difficult position. So you're caught between three competing loans. Which one are you prioritising right now?

Customer: The ICICI home loan, na. That one I have to pay first. The bank manager made it very clear that if I miss even one EMI, they will start recovery proceedings immediately. So that one comes first, always. The business loan from Axis, I'm also trying to keep that current because I have a personal guarantee on it. Your loan from Credix, sir, I... <interruption> ...I'm very sorry, but I have to keep that on the back burner for now. I cannot manage all three.

Agent: Sir, I understand the pressure you're under. But let me ask — are you currently paying both the ICICI and Axis loans on time, or are you falling behind on those as well?

Customer: ICICI one, yes, I manage that somehow. The Axis loan, I missed one EMI about a month back, but I caught up this month. So we are okay there. But sir, honestly, I cannot... I really cannot manage all three simultaneously. Something has to give, and right now it's your loan.

Agent: Understood, sir. What you're describing is what we call an overindebtedness situation — when your total EMI burden exceeds your monthly income and you're forced to prioritise one lender over another. This is actually quite common, and we do have options. Instead of pushing you for immediate payment today, what if we look at restructuring your loan with us? We could reduce your EMI for a few months or extend the tenure so you can manage all three without defaulting everywhere.

Customer: Restructure? Is that even possible? How long would it take, sir? And what's the guarantee that it will actually happen?

Agent: It is very much possible, sir. We have a hardship restructure program specifically for situations like yours. I will submit your case to our approval team, and it typically takes 3 to 5 working days for a decision. But sir, I want to ask — can you commit to at least a partial payment while we process this? Even Rs. 10,000 this month would demonstrate good faith and strengthen your case when we present it to the approval team.

Customer: Rs. 10,000? <interruption> ...let me see. When would you need this by?

Agent: Can you arrange it by the end of this week? That's in four days. By Friday, if possible.

Customer: Haan, Friday maybe I can do. But sir, I have to be honest with you — I cannot promise anything beyond that. My wife has a doctor's appointment on Wednesday, and my car needs servicing. So I'm a bit stretched. But maybe, maybe I can arrange Rs. 10,000 by Friday evening. But this is not a solution, sir. The EMI itself needs to come down. Can you reduce it to Rs. 12,000 or Rs. 13,000 per month?

Agent: That's a fair request, sir. I cannot guarantee a specific reduction right now, but when I submit your case for restructure, I will definitely request that your EMI be brought down to around Rs. 13,000 per month. That would bring your total EMI load to approximately Rs. 46,500, which should be manageable with your current income.

Customer: Okay, okay. So you will submit the restructure case, and I will try to pay Rs. 10,000 by Friday. But sir, I'm not making any promise beyond that until the restructure is approved. Is that clear?

Agent: Absolutely clear, sir. Let me just confirm your contact details. The number we have on file is 9876543210. Is that still correct?

Customer: Yes, that's correct. But you can also reach me on my wife's number — 9988776655 — if I'm not picking up.

Agent: Perfect. I've noted both numbers. Sir, I will personally flag your restructure request as urgent given the overindebtedness situation. You should hear from our approval team within 5 working days. In the meantime, Rs. 10,000 by Friday. Can we confirm that?

Customer: Yes, Friday I can manage. Thank you for understanding, sir. I was really worried about this call.

Agent: You did the right thing by picking up and being honest about your situation, sir. We will take care of this. Have a good day.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh. Who is calling?

Agent: Hello Rajesh, this is Priya from Collections at FinServe Credit. I'm calling regarding your loan account with us — account number 2847-9156-FL. Do you have a few minutes to speak?

Customer: Haan, haan, I know about the loan. What is it? I have been paying my EMIs on time mostly.

Agent: Thank you for that. I can see your account is currently showing an outstanding amount of 47,850 rupees against an EMI of 8,500 that was due on the 15th of last month. Can we discuss your repayment plan?

Customer: Wait, 47,850? That does not sound correct to me. According to my records, I should only owe around 25,000 rupees. I have been checking my statements and I have made all my payments. Why is the amount so high?

Agent: I understand your concern, Rajesh. Let me pull up your detailed ledger. One moment please... Okay, I can see the last payment we received was on the 8th of December for 8,500. Before that, you made a payment on the 5th of November. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, yes, that is correct. But you see, the amount you are showing now includes so much extra interest and some charges I don't even recognize. I am looking at my bank statement right now and I have not defaulted. Why am I being charged all these penalties and extra interest?

Agent: I see. So you are disputing the interest and penalty charges that have been added to your account?

Customer: Exactly! Not just that, but I am also concerned about how this is being reported to the credit bureau. My CIBIL score has dropped significantly, and I believe the way you are reporting this account is incorrect. The status on the bureau shows I am seriously delinquent, but I have been making regular payments. This is damaging my credit profile unfairly.

Agent: I understand, Rajesh. This is an important point. Are you saying the credit bureau report does not accurately reflect your payment history?

Customer: Yes, exactly! The bureau is showing this account as defaulted and delinquent for the past two months, but I have paid every single EMI on time except for maybe one that was delayed by a few days. I want this corrected before I make any further payments. How can I pay more money when the bureau is reporting me incorrectly? This will affect my chances of getting another loan or a credit card in the future.

Agent: I completely understand your frustration, Rajesh. The credit bureau reporting is a serious concern. To help you, I will need to escalate this to our verification team. They will review your exact payment history against what has been reported to CIBIL and the other bureaus. Can you confirm your current address so I can log this escalation properly?

Customer: My address is 42-B, Sector 7, Noida, Uttar Pradesh, 201301. But listen, I need this resolved before I can proceed with any payment. I don't want to pay an inflated amount and then have this false reporting continue to hurt my credit score. Can you guarantee that you will correct the bureau records?

Agent: Rajesh, I appreciate the urgency. I cannot guarantee a bureau correction on this call, but I can assure you that once our team verifies your payment records and confirms the discrepancy, we will initiate a formal correction request with CIBIL and other relevant bureaus. This process typically takes 15 to 20 days. In the meantime, can we discuss a payment plan for the amount you acknowledge you owe?

Customer: No, I don't want to commit to anything until this is sorted. How do I know what the correct amount is? I need a corrected statement from you showing what I actually owe after you verify the payments. Then I will decide on the payment. I cannot pay based on an incorrect amount. This entire situation is very frustrating.

Agent: That is completely fair, Rajesh. I will mark your account for an urgent verification and ledger correction. Our team will contact you within 48 hours with a corrected statement. Once you receive that, we can discuss the accurate outstanding amount and work out a repayment plan. Does that work for you?

Customer: Yes, that is better. But please make sure this verification is thorough and honest. And I want this bureau issue addressed as a priority. My credit is at stake here.

Agent: Absolutely, Rajesh. I have noted all of this on your file. Your account reference is 2847-9156-FL, and I am flagging this for immediate review by our verification team. They will send you a corrected ledger and initiate the bureau correction process. You should expect contact within 48 hours. Is there anything else I should note?

Customer: Just make sure this gets done properly. And please, no more calls until I hear from your verification team with the corrected statement. I don't want to be called multiple times about an incorrect amount.

Agent: Understood, Rajesh. I have added a note that you should not receive collection calls until the verification is complete. Thank you for your patience, and we will be in touch very soon with the resolution.

Customer: Okay, thank you.

Agent: Thank you, Rajesh. Have a good day.

transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Priya from Fintech Credit. I am calling regarding your loan account ending in 4827. Your EMI of rupees 12,500 was due on the 15th of this month, and it appears we have not received payment yet. Can we discuss this?

Customer: <interruption> Yes, yes, I know about this. Look, I have been meaning to call you people actually. The situation is very difficult right now.

Agent: I understand. Can you tell me what is happening? Are you facing any challenges with the payment?

Customer: Rajesh here is actually not working right now. I mean, I was working at a manufacturing company in Noida — Hindustan Steel Industries — for the last eight years. But two months back, the company closed down suddenly. Just like that, no notice, no severance. They said there was some financial crisis and they had to shut operations. So around three hundred workers, we all lost our jobs on the same day.

Agent: I see. That's very difficult, Rajesh. So you have been unemployed for two months now?

Customer: Haan, two months exactly. I have been looking for work, but you know how it is. The market is very slow. Everyone is asking for experience in new software systems, and I have only done manual production line work. My savings are almost finished now. I used them for household expenses, my daughter's school fees, and... and some medical bills for my mother.

Agent: Understood. And during this time, have you been able to make any payments toward your loan?

Customer: No, nothing. I could not. I have been trying to take some small work here and there — some contract jobs, some labor work — but the money is very irregular. Some weeks I get two thousand rupees, some weeks nothing. How can I commit to a 12,500 rupee EMI when I don't even know if I will have food money next week?

Agent: Yes, I hear you. What is your current situation? Do you have any immediate income expected, or are you still searching for a permanent role?

Customer: Still searching, yaar. I have applied to maybe twenty, thirty companies, but nothing is confirmed yet. One company called me for an interview next week for a supervisor position — it pays around twenty-five thousand per month if I get it — but nothing is sure right now. The interview is on the 18th of next month.

Agent: That sounds promising, Rajesh. Let me ask you — if you do get this job and the salary starts coming in, when do you think you could start making payments again?

Customer: <interruption> If I get the job, yes, then I can start. The first salary usually comes after thirty days or so, maybe by mid-month after I join. So if I join on the 18th, I could have money by middle of... mid-February maybe? But I cannot promise anything right now because the interview is not even done yet.

Agent: I understand your situation is uncertain. Let me check your account details. Your outstanding balance is currently rupees 87,400, which includes your overdue EMI and some late fees that have been added. Given your employment situation, what we can do is see if we can structure something temporary. Have you considered requesting a moratorium or a temporary reduction in your EMI while you find employment?

Customer: Moratorium? What is that exactly? You mean they will not take any payment from me for some time?

Agent: Yes, exactly. A moratorium means we pause the EMI payments for a period — typically two to three months — while you stabilize your income. After that, either your EMI would resume, or we might extend the loan tenure to spread the remaining balance over a longer period.

Customer: Hmm, that could help. But will there be more charges added? Interest and penalties and all?

Agent: That is something we would need to assess with our approval team. Generally, during a moratorium, interest continues to accrue, but we would waive the late fees. I cannot promise anything without proper approval, but your hardship situation — job loss — definitely qualifies you for consideration.

Customer: <interruption> Okay, okay. So what do I need to do? How long will this take?

Agent: What I will do is escalate your case as a hardship request to our senior team. They will review your employment situation and see what relief options we can provide. In the meantime, I need some information from you. Can you confirm your current address? Is it still Flat 24, Ashok Nagar, Delhi-110092?

Customer: Yes, that is correct. Same address.

Agent: Good. And your contact number — is this the best number to reach you?

Customer: Yes, this is my personal number. Please call on this only.

Agent: Perfect. Rajesh, I will submit your case for hardship review today itself. You should expect a call from our senior collections officer within two to three business days. They will discuss the moratorium option and any other restructuring possibilities. In the meantime, try to keep your contact details updated with us. When you have confirmation about the job, you can call us back immediately and let us know.

Customer: Okay, thank you. But one more thing — I have been getting calls every day, sometimes twice a day. I understand I am late, but it is causing me stress. Can you reduce the call frequency?

Agent: That is fair. I will make a note on your account to reduce the call frequency while your hardship case is under review. You will hear from us once the senior team has made a decision. Is there anything else you need to clarify?

Customer: No, that is all. Thank you for understanding my situation.

Agent: Thank you for being honest with me, Rajesh. We will be in touch within three business days. Take care.

Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh. Who is calling?

Agent: Rajesh, this is Priya from Horizon Finance. I'm calling regarding your personal loan account ending in 4782. Do you have a few minutes to speak with me?

Customer: Uh, yes, but I already told someone last month that I cannot pay right now. My business was affected because of the lockdown situation, na. The EMI is 18,500 rupees and I am still... I am still waiting for things to improve.

Agent: I completely understand, Rajesh. I can see from your file that your last payment was in September. That was almost four months ago now. Your current outstanding balance is 1,84,350 rupees including interest. I wanted to discuss some options with you today. Have you been able to save anything in the last month or so?

Customer: <interruption> Look, I don't have 1,84,000 right now. That is too much. My business is just starting again, the cash flow is very slow. I think... I think the amount you are showing is wrong because I have paid some amount in between also.

Agent: Okay, let me help you with that. Can you tell me which payments you made? I can verify them and adjust the balance accordingly.

Customer: I paid around 20,000 in November through my friend's account. He transferred it to the bank. But I don't have the reference number now. I am telling you the amount is higher than what I actually owe.

Agent: Thank you for clarifying that, Rajesh. Let me note that down. Once I verify that payment, your balance may be lower. But even with that adjustment, you would still have a significant amount outstanding. Here is what I want to propose. Since your business is recovering, what if we structure a settlement? Instead of paying the full outstanding amount, you could pay a reduced lump sum amount, and we can close this account. This would also help your credit profile going forward.

Customer: <interruption> Settlement? How much are you talking about? I cannot afford... I mean, what is the amount you are asking for?

Agent: Based on your situation and the pending verification of that November payment, I would suggest a settlement of around 1,20,000 rupees. This is a significant reduction from the full outstanding. You could pay this in two instalments if that helps — 60,000 now and the remaining 60,000 within 45 days. What do you think?

Customer: Sixty thousand now? That is still... okay, let me think. When is my next salary coming? My salary usually comes on the 15th of every month. If I wait until next month, I can manage 60,000 from that. And then after two months, I can give the second instalment. But I need the settlement letter from you first to confirm this is final.

Agent: That is a very reasonable approach, Rajesh. So you are agreeing to pay 60,000 on or before the 15th of next month, and then 60,000 more within 45 days after that, correct? And this settlement would close the account completely?

Customer: Yes, yes, that is correct. But only if you send me the settlement letter showing this amount is final and there are no more interest charges or penalties after this. I don't want any surprises later.

Agent: Perfect. I will generate a formal settlement sanction letter for you today itself. It will clearly state that upon receipt of these two payments totalling 1,20,000, your account will be fully settled and closed. No further interest or penalties will accrue. I will send this to your email and also via SMS. Once you receive and confirm receipt, we can place your account on hold and you can proceed with the payments as planned.

Customer: Okay, that sounds good. You will email it to me? My email is rajesh.kumar1985 at gmail dot com.

Agent: Yes, confirmed. Rajesh.kumar1985 at gmail dot com. I will send the sanction letter within two hours. You should also receive an SMS with a link. Once you confirm receipt and acceptance, your account will be placed on hold and marked as settlement agreed. You will not receive any more collection calls after that. Does that work for you?

Customer: Yes, that is perfect. I will look out for the email. And I will arrange the first 60,000 by the 15th. Thank you for understanding my situation.

Agent: Thank you, Rajesh. I really appreciate your cooperation. We have successfully agreed to settle your account for 1,20,000 in two tranches. The sanction letter will be your confirmation. Please watch for it and confirm receipt. If you have any questions, you can call me back at this number. Your account is now marked as settlement agreed and we will be in touch once we receive your first payment. Thank you and best of luck with your business recovery.

transcript:
Agent: Good afternoon, am I speaking with Arjun Verma?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Arjun. Who is calling?

Agent: Arjun, this is Vikram from the collections team at FinanceHub Credit. I'm calling regarding your loan account, the one ending in 5639. Do you have a moment to speak?

Customer: <interruption> Yes, yes, I know about this. Look, I have been very busy with work. The EMI was due on the 15th of last month and I know I am late. But things have been very tight, yaar.

Agent: I understand, Arjun. According to our records, your outstanding balance is currently Rs 47,890, which includes the missed EMI of Rs 12,500 plus some late fees. Can we discuss a payment plan that works for you?

Customer: Forty-seven thousand? That sounds very high. When I last checked, it was only around 35,000 or so. Are you sure about this figure? The interest charges seem very high.

Agent: Let me clarify that for you. Your original EMI is Rs 12,500 per month. You've missed two months now — so that's Rs 25,000 in EMIs. Then there are interest accruals of about Rs 9,500 and a late fee of Rs 890. That brings us to Rs 47,890. Does that make sense?

Customer: Okay, okay, I see. So the interest is quite a bit. But listen, I cannot pay the full amount right now. My salary usually comes on the 25th of the month. What if I pay you Rs 15,000 tomorrow? I can arrange that. Then after my salary comes, I can pay another Rs 20,000 by the 26th of this month. That leaves some balance, but at least I am starting to pay, no?

Agent: That's a good start, Arjun. So you're proposing Rs 15,000 tomorrow and then Rs 20,000 after your salary arrives on the 25th. That's Rs 35,000 in total. There would still be a remaining balance of about Rs 12,890. Are you willing to commit to clearing that balance by the 10th of next month?

Customer: Yes, I can do that. By the 10th of next month, I will pay the remaining amount. I give you my word on this.

Agent: Excellent, Arjun. Let me confirm the commitment with you. Tomorrow you will pay Rs 15,000. On the 26th of this month, you will pay Rs 20,000. And by the 10th of next month, you will clear the remaining balance of Rs 12,890. Is that correct?

Customer: Yes, that is correct. But one thing — can you send me a payment link? I prefer to pay through UPI. And also, can you note down my alternate number? My phone has been giving problems, so I am using my wife's number sometimes. It's 9876543210. Can you add that?

Agent: Absolutely, Arjun. I will send you a payment link via SMS right away. And I have noted down your alternate contact number as 9876543210. Let me also confirm your current address is still Flat 12, Ashok Nagar, Delhi — 110052. Is that still correct?

Customer: Yes, yes, that is correct. The address is the same. Okay, I will wait for the payment link. And I promise you, I will make these payments on time. This has been stressful, but now at least I have a plan.

Agent: Thank you for your commitment, Arjun. Just to recap: first payment of Rs 15,000 tomorrow via the link I'm sending, second payment of Rs 20,000 on the 26th, and final payment of Rs 12,890 by the 10th of next month. transcript:
Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Sharma?

Customer: Yes, this is Rajesh. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Akshay from Capital Loans collection team. I'm calling regarding your account with us. Do you have a few minutes to speak?

Customer: Look, I don't know why you people keep calling. I've already settled this loan, okay? This is the third time someone from your company is calling me.

Agent: I understand your frustration, Rajesh. Let me just verify the account quickly. Your loan reference number is CL-2024-087543, and the outstanding amount we have on record is Rs 2,47,500 against the original amount of Rs 5 lakhs. Can you confirm if this is correct?

Customer: No, no, no. This is wrong. I don't have any outstanding. I closed this loan already. I got the NOC from you people back in... it was around June, I think. I paid the final amount and they sent me the closure letter. I have it at home somewhere.

Agent: Okay, Rajesh, I appreciate you sharing that. Let me check our records here. <pause> So you're saying you received a No Objection Certificate from us? That would mean the loan was fully settled and closed. Can you tell me when exactly you made the final payment?

Customer: Yes, yes, exactly. I made the last payment in June. It was after the salary came in. I think it was... maybe June 15th or so. My wife was also involved in that transaction, we did a bank transfer. NEFT, I think. Or maybe IMPS, I'm not sure now.

Agent: Right. And did you keep the receipt or reference number from that transfer?

Customer: The receipt, hmm, I don't have it right now, but like I said, I have the NOC letter at home. It clearly says the loan is closed and there's no further liability. So I'm confused why you're calling me for Rs 2,47,500 when the account should be zero.

Agent: I completely understand, Rajesh. And I apologize for the inconvenience. But I need to be honest with you — our system is still showing an active outstanding balance. It's possible there was a delay in the closure being reflected in our database, or <interruption>

Customer: Look, this is ridiculous. Why would I lie about this? I have the NOC. The account is closed. You're saying my payment didn't go through? That's your system's problem, not mine. I paid in good faith. I don't owe you anything.

Agent: I hear you, and I'm not suggesting you're lying at all. What I'm saying is that sometimes there's a lag between when a final payment is received and when our closure team processes the account and updates the system. It happens. But before we can confirm that the account is indeed closed, I need to verify the payment details. Can you help me with that?

Customer: How do I help you verify? I told you I paid in June. I don't have the reference number on me right now. And frankly, it shouldn't be my responsibility to track this down. You people should have your records in order. If I got an NOC, the loan is closed. That's the whole point of an NOC, isn't it?

Agent: You're absolutely right, Rajesh. The NOC is the proof of closure. What I'd like to do is this — can you send me a photo or a copy of that NOC letter when you get a chance? Once I have that, I can immediately escalate it to our records team and they can match it against your payment details in our system. That way, we can clear this up properly and remove your account from our collections list.

Customer: Okay, fine. I can do that. But this is frustrating. I've already done my part. Now I have to run around and find the letter and send it to you? This is poor service.

Agent: I absolutely agree, Rajesh, and I apologize for that. I know it's an inconvenience. Once you send the NOC, we'll prioritize it on our end. In the meantime, let me just confirm — have you received any other communication from us after June, or is this the first time we've contacted you since then?

Customer: No, you haven't called since then. Or I don't remember anyway. But that's because the loan was closed, so there was no reason to call. Now suddenly you're calling with a big outstanding amount. It doesn't make sense.

Agent: That's a fair point. And I apologize again. Rajesh, I'm going to note on your account right now that you've provided us with notice of an NOC and a closure claim. Once you send that letter, our records team will verify it against our closure and settlement logs. If everything matches up, the account will be cleared immediately and you won't hear from us again.

Customer: Okay. Good. I'll find the letter and send it to you. But I'm telling you, I don't owe anything. The account is closed. I shouldn't have to keep explaining this.

Agent: Understood, Rajesh. I've got that noted. Thank you for your patience, and I apologize again for the trouble. We'll resolve this as soon as we receive the NOC.

Agent: Namaste, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar? This is Priya calling from Zenith Finance regarding your loan account ending in 4782.

Customer: <interruption> Legal notice? What legal notice? I... I didn't see anything like that.

Agent: Sir, the notice was regarding your outstanding EMI of Rs 42,500 which is now 127 days overdue. The original due date was the 10th of September. Are you aware of this account status?

Customer: Haan, haan, I know about the EMI. But the notice... I got some letter from some court, but I thought it was... I don't know, some spam thing. My wife was handling the post.

Agent: Sir, this is not spam. This is a formal legal notice from our legal team. The court has issued a summons in your case. We need to understand — have you received any official court document? Any summons or notice with a court stamp?

Customer: <interruption> Court? No, no, no. This is getting... I mean, I got a letter but I didn't read it properly. The letter is still in the house somewhere. Mujhe nahi pata it was from the court. What does this mean? Will they arrest me or something?

Agent: Sir, please don't panic. The legal process has begun because the loan is significantly overdue. But there is still a way to stop this. If you can settle the outstanding amount or make a commitment to pay, we can halt the legal proceedings. Can you tell me — what is your current situation? Why haven't you been able to pay the EMI?

Customer: Situation is difficult, Priya. My company gave us a salary cut in August. Thirty percent cut. I was managing okay before, but now I have the house loan also, and my wife's medical treatment. Sab kuch pressure hai.

Agent: I understand, sir. This is a difficult time. But the court proceedings will only make things worse. Let me ask you directly — if we can work out a settlement amount, something less than the full 42,500, can you pay it? Or if we break it into smaller installments, is that possible?

Customer: Settlement? What kind of settlement? How much are you talking about? And when would I have to pay? Because my salary is only coming on the 25th of next month. Right now I have maybe 15,000 in the account.

Agent: Sir, a settlement would reduce the total amount you owe. Instead of 42,500 plus the legal costs and interest that are accruing, we could potentially settle for 38,000. But this needs to be paid as soon as possible — ideally within 7 to 10 days — to stop the court proceedings from moving forward. Can you do that after your salary comes on the 25th?

Customer: <interruption> 38,000? That's still a lot. And the legal thing... if I pay, will they really stop? Because I am very worried about this now. I have never been in any legal case before. I don't understand how this works.

Agent: Yes, sir. If you agree to the settlement and make the payment, we will immediately file a withdrawal with the court. The case will be closed. But you must act quickly. The next court date is in 12 days. So if we can get your commitment today and payment by the 25th, we can prevent the case from going further. Do you understand?

Customer: Haan, I understand. But I need to think about this. And I need to talk to my wife. The medical bills are still coming, and I don't know if 38,000 is something we can manage right now. Can you... can you call me next week? After I have spoken to her and looked at what we can actually do?

Agent: Sir, I can call you next week, but I must be clear — every day the case is moving forward. The court is not waiting. If you can commit to a settlement figure right now, even if you can't pay immediately, it will protect you. Can you at least commit to paying 38,000 by the 25th? That gives you time to arrange the funds with your wife's input.

Customer: <interruption> I... I want to settle this. I really do. But I can't promise 38,000 without talking to my wife first. And I need to understand what happens if I can't pay by the 25th. What happens then? Will they... will they come to my house? Will there be more trouble?

Agent: Sir, if the settlement is agreed and you don't pay by the committed date, the legal process will continue and may escalate to a recovery agent visit or auction proceedings. That is why I am advising you to commit today. Speak to your wife immediately — tonight if possible — and call me back within 24 hours. Can you do that?

Customer: Okay. Okay. I will talk to my wife tonight. And I will call you back tomorrow. But I want to be very clear — I am not refusing to pay. I am just... I need to know that my family is safe, you understand? I need to know what this legal thing means for my house and my job.

Agent: I understand, sir. Let me note that you are aware of the legal proceedings and you are open to settling the matter. I will make a note that you will call back within 24 hours with your wife's input. In the meantime, please locate that legal notice letter and read it carefully. It will have all the details. And sir, please do take this seriously. The court process is real and time-sensitive.

Customer: Yes, I will find the letter and read it. And I will call you tomorrow. Thank you for explaining it. I was very scared when you said court, but now I understand better. I will call you back.

Agent: Thank you, sir. I will be waiting for your call. Take care.

Agent: Namaste, good afternoon. Am I speaking with Arun Menon?

Customer: Haan, speaking. But who is this? I am in the middle of something right now.

Agent: Arun, I am calling from Fintech Loans. Your account number ending in 7843 — haan, I have your file here. Your outstanding balance is 2,12,500 rupees and the payment was due on the 10th. So I wanted to understand what is happening with your account, na?

Customer: Haan, I know about the payment. <interruption> But listen, you see, there was a big situation here in Kochi. The monsoon floods last month — they affected everything. My house, my workplace, everything is damaged. The water level was very high, and we had to run away quickly. We lost so much.

Agent: Oh, I see. That is difficult. But Arun, before we discuss the situation, let me confirm your address na. You are staying at Plot 47, Panampilly Nagar, Kochi, 682036? Is this still correct?

Customer: Yes, yes, that is correct. But listen, the house itself — the ground floor got flooded. The walls are wet, the furniture is damaged. I am staying upstairs for now, but we need repairs badly.

Agent: Okay, I have noted that your address matches our records. Now, you mentioned the flood affected your work also?

Customer: Yes, exactly. I was running a small spice export business from a warehouse in Ernakulathappan. The entire inventory — tonnes of cardamom, pepper, cloves — everything got soaked and spoiled. The machinery also got damaged. The business is completely closed right now. I am waiting for the insurance settlement. It is taking time, you know. They are asking for so much documentation.

Agent: How much are you expecting from the insurance, roughly?

Customer: I have filed a claim for about 25 lakhs. But the insurance company is asking for more evidence, more photographs, more bills. They are saying it will take at least two more months. Maybe three months. Until then, I have no income from the business.

Agent: So right now, what income are you getting, Arun?

Customer: Right now? <interruption> I am doing whatever I can find. Some days I am helping my neighbor with his wholesale vegetable business — maybe I get 5,000 or 6,000 rupees. Some days I am doing online delivery work, Blinkit and all. Maybe another 8,000 or 10,000 per month. So total is maybe 12,000 to 15,000 rupees if I am lucky. But before the flood, the business was giving me 70,000 to 80,000 monthly.

Agent: I understand. So this is a very sudden drop in your income. And when do you expect the salary — sorry, when do you expect the insurance to come through?

Customer: <interruption> The insurance company said minimum two months from now. Maybe by August-end or September. They are very slow. I have been calling them every week. But I cannot speed them up, na.

Agent: Right. And meanwhile, your expenses are still the same?

Customer: No, no, my expenses are more now. I am spending on house repairs — I have already spent 2 lakhs on fixing the walls and the foundation. I still need another 1.5 lakhs for the roof and the windows. My wife is also saying the kitchen needs work. And then there are school fees for the children, groceries, medicines — everything is tight. Very tight. I am not avoiding your loan, but right now I cannot find 2 lakh rupees from somewhere.

Agent: Arun, I completely understand. This is a natural disaster situation. You have lost your business, your home is damaged, and you are waiting for insurance. This is genuine hardship. I am going to mark your account as hardship case due to natural disaster — flood damage. We will not pursue aggressive collection right now. Instead, our hardship team will contact you, maybe after one week, to understand better and see if we can restructure your loan or give you a moratorium period.

Customer: That sounds good. But I want to be clear — I am not running away from the loan. Once the insurance money comes, I will pay everything. I will clear your 2,12,500 and also my other debts.

Agent: Yes, I understand. You have mentioned you are waiting for the insurance settlement. We will note that down. And Arun, once the insurance comes through, you can call us directly, haan? We will process your payment quickly.

Customer: Yes, yes, I will do that. Thank you for understanding. I was worried you would be very aggressive.

Agent: No, no, Arun. We are not here to make your situation worse. You are in a difficult time. Our team will contact you soon to help. Take care of yourself and your family.

Customer: Thank you. I appreciate it. Goodbye.

Agent: Goodbye, Arun. All the best.

Agent: Hello, am I speaking with Rajesh Kumar?

Customer: Haan, yes, this is Rajesh speaking. Who is calling?

Agent: Hi Rajesh, this is Amit from Sundar Finance. We're calling regarding your loan account ending in 4521. You have an outstanding balance of Rs. 1,84,500 that's now 45 days overdue. Your last payment was made on March 15th. Can we discuss your repayment plan today?

Customer: Haan, I know about this. See, I am aware, but the situation is very difficult right now. Very difficult.

Agent: I understand. Can you tell me what's happening? What's the challenge you're facing?

Customer: Actually, Amit, you see, my entire business got affected. I have a small textiles business in Surat — I import fabrics and materials from Gujarat suppliers. But three weeks back, there was a major flood in the area. The warehouse where I was keeping all my stock, the entire inventory got destroyed. Everything. Lakhs of rupees of stock just... gone.

Agent: Oh no, I'm very sorry to hear that. That's a serious situation. <interruption> Can you tell me more about when this happened and what the impact has been on your business?

Customer: It happened on April 2nd. The water level rose so much, no one expected it like this. Insurance company is saying they will cover some portion, but the claim process is very slow, very slow. They are asking for so many documents, surveys, everything. It will take two, three months at least. Meanwhile, my business has completely stopped. No stock means no sales, Amit. I cannot fulfill any orders.

Agent: Yes, I can see how that would impact your cash flow significantly. Have you been able to restart operations at all, or is the business completely halted?

Customer: Completely halted, yaar. I have also taken loans from other suppliers on credit, and they are also pressuring me now. One bank, they are also calling for another EMI I have. So many obligations. But without the stock, I cannot generate any income to pay anyone. The insurance payout is my only hope right now, but it will take time.

Agent: <interruption> I understand, Rajesh. This is clearly an external event that's beyond your control. Do you have an estimated timeline from the insurance company for when the claim might be settled?

Customer: They are saying by end of June, maybe early July. They have given me a provisional estimate of about Rs. 1,20,000 to Rs. 1,40,000. But I don't know exactly when the money will come. Could be July, could be August.

Agent: Okay. And your warehouse, has it been assessed by them yet?

Customer: Yes, they sent a surveyor last week. He has documented everything. Now they are processing the claim. But the paperwork is very slow. I have submitted everything they asked for — photographs, receipts, invoices, everything.

Agent: Rajesh, given that your business has been impacted by this flood and you're awaiting an insurance settlement, I want to help you find a way forward. We cannot keep this account in default, but I understand your situation is temporary. Once you receive the insurance payout, would you be in a position to clear this EMI and any other pending dues?

Customer: <interruption> Yes, yes, absolutely. Once the insurance money comes, that will be my first priority. I will clear this loan immediately. I promise you. But right now, I have no money. Even to buy food, I am struggling. My family is dependent on me, and this flood has just destroyed everything.

Agent: I hear you. This is clearly a hardship situation caused by the natural disaster. What I can do is escalate this to my supervisor for a possible moratorium or payment holiday until your insurance claim is settled. But I need to understand — do you have any other source of income right now, or any savings you could use?

Customer: No, no savings. I have some family members who are helping me with daily expenses, but I cannot ask them for such a large amount. And right now, no other income source. The business was my only income.

Agent: Understood. I'm going to escalate your case to our collections manager as a hardship case due to natural disaster impact. We may be able to offer you a pause on EMI collections until you receive your insurance settlement. However, I need to document your situation properly. Can you provide me with some proof of the flood damage and the insurance claim? A copy of the claim lodging receipt or the surveyor's report?

Customer: Yes, I can send you copies. I have the claim reference number from the insurance company. I also have photographs of the damaged warehouse and the stock. I can WhatsApp these to you or email them.

Agent: Perfect. Please send those to me at amit.collections@sundarfinance.com. Include the insurance claim reference, the surveyor's report if you have it, and any correspondence from the insurance company regarding the claim timeline. Once I have these documents, I will escalate to our hardship team and we will get back to you within two business days with a decision.

Customer: Okay, I will send everything today itself. When will you call me back?

Agent: We will call you back within two business days once we review your documentation. In the meantime, please do not make any payment — just let us know once your insurance settlement is processed. Rajesh, I want you to know that we understand this is beyond your control. We will try to help.

Customer: Thank you, Amit. I appreciate this. I really hope this gets resolved quickly. This situation is very stressful.

Agent: I understand. We will be in touch within two business days. Stay safe, and please send those documents at your earliest convenience.

Customer: Yes, thank you. I will send them today.

Agent: Thank you, Rajesh. Goodbye.
